sources.entry: OmniRoute - Self-hostable AI gateway with 4-tier cascading fallback and multi-provider load balancing. Supports 200+ models across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and local providers.

summary.one_liner: OmniRoute is a self-hostable AI gateway that exposes one OpenAI-compatible endpoint and routes requests across many providers with combos, automatic fallback, and free-tier aggregation.
summary.what_it_does: It runs as a local or self-hosted server (npm, Docker, Bun, or from source) that provides an OpenAI-compatible /v1 API and a dashboard for connecting your own provider accounts. Requests can target a specific model or the "auto" model, which builds a virtual combo from connected providers and scores them live on factors such as quota, cost, latency and health. Users can also build combos with 20 routing strategies (priority, round-robin, cost-optimized, quota-weighted, fusion, pipeline and others) and chain fallbacks across layers. The README describes a prompt compression pipeline of up to 12 engines, a per-combo token-saving option, MCP and A2A endpoints for agents, a CLI with commands to launch or configure tools like Claude Code, Codex and Aider, and a dashboard page that catalogs third-party free tiers. The README's headline figures (377 providers, 1,475 model IDs, and a free-tier token estimate) are self-reported by the project.
use_cases: route one API endpoint to many AI providers
automatic fallback when a model or provider fails
run coding agents like Claude Code or Codex through a single gateway
compress prompts to cut token usage
self-host an OpenAI-compatible proxy with a dashboard
how_to_run: docker run -d --name omniroute --restart unless-stopped -p 127.0.0.1:20128:20128 -v omniroute-data:/app/data diegosouzapw/omniroute:latest
notable: Combo routing with 20 strategies and an auto model that scores connected providers live
Free-tier catalog and dashboard page estimating pooled free quotas across providers
Built-in MCP (stdio, HTTP, SSE) and A2A endpoints so agents can control the gateway
CLI that launches or configures coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Aider and Goose
Prompt compression stack of 12 engines with presets such as Lite, Standard and Ultra
caveats: Requires bringing your own provider accounts and API keys; free tiers are controlled by each provider and can change
Coding-agent workloads need a large heap; the Docker image defaults to 1024 MB and the README recommends 8 GB or more for heavy use
npm 11+ may block required postinstall scripts, so specific packages must be allowed during install
keywords: share one api key across tools
use free ai models for coding
